Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of 2025 service arrangements and grant aid agreements, Part 1 and Part 2/HPSR, which had not been countersigned by the HSE at 31 December 2025, by arrangement type and HSE region; the total funding released to agencies in the absence of a fully executed agreement; and the status at the date of reply of the agreements with the bodies, in tabular form. [76370/26]

1919. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the current operational status of the designated regional endometriosis hub in Galway; whether a clinical lead has been appointed; the number and grades of specialist staff currently assigned to the service; the specialist diagnostic and surgical services presently available; the reasons for a delay in making the hub fully operational; and the expected date on which a comprehensive regional service will be established. [76225/26]

1920. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the interim arrangements in place for patients in Galway, Mayo, Roscommon, Sligo, Donegal and the wider western region who require specialist endometriosis assessment or surgery that is not currently available in Galway; whether patients can access designated centres elsewhere in the State irrespective of geographical catchment boundaries; and the measures being taken to ensure that patients are not refused access due to their place of residence. [76226/26]

1922. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of consultant gynaecologists currently providing specialist endometriosis excision surgery nationally; the number of multidisciplinary teams with access to colorectal and urological surgical expertise; the current recruitment status of vacant specialist posts in Galway; and whether additional funding or staffing approvals are required to establish a fully operational service. [76228/26]

1923. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of patients currently awaiting endometriosis-related outpatient assessment and surgery, respectively, nationally and by hospital; the number awaiting complex excision surgery; the average and longest waiting times; whether the HSE maintains a dedicated national dataset on endometriosis referrals and treatment; and whether plans exist to establish comprehensive reporting on patient demand and treatment capacity. [76227/26]

1925. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of applications received, approved, refused and completed under the endometriosis scheme abroad since its establishment, broken down by region where available; the eligibility and consultant referral requirements; and the arrangements in place for patients who cannot access a suitably qualified consultant to support an application. [76229/26]

1927. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the progress made in implementing the national endometriosis framework at each designated regional and supra-regional centre; the funding allocated and expended to date; the implementation milestones achieved and outstanding; the clinical education and public awareness measures introduced; and whether the HSE intends to publish regular progress reports on implementation. [76230/26]

769. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether the SMS reminder systems in use across hospitals are configured as one-way reminder services or include two-way communication functionality allowing patients to confirm, cancel or reschedule appointments; to provide a breakdown by hospital; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [36438/26]

770. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the cost per SMS message incurred by each hospital or healthcare facility based on the provider or system in use; the total expenditure on SMS appointment reminders in the most recent twelve-month period; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [36439/26]

771. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of outpatient appointment reminder SMS messages issued by each hospital or healthcare facility in the past three months; to provide this information on a per-hospital basis; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [36440/26]

772. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the extent to which SMS reminder systems are actively utilised across hospitals, including a comparison of usage levels between sites; whether any hospitals with access to such systems are not making full use of them; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [36441/26]

798. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the level of access to primary care services for older people in rural areas; including physiotherapy and community-based supports; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [51292/26]

799. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if an assessment has been carried out on the cumulative cost burden of healthcare for older people, including GP care, prescriptions, vaccines, and screening services; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [51293/26]

193. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the extent of the use of SMS messaging systems for outpatient appointment reminders across public hospitals and healthcare facilities; the number of messages issued and level of utilisation by each site; whether all facilities with access to such systems are making full use of them; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [47996/26]

385. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if she is aware of delays in accessing first antenatal appointments at University Hospital Galway, with women now reportedly waiting until 16–17 weeks gestation rather than the standard 12-week timeframe; the reasons for these delays; the risks posed to maternal and foetal health, particularly for high-risk pregnancies; and the steps she is taking to ensure timely and safe antenatal care for women across the UHG catchment area. [33109/26]

3070. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the measures the HSE has in place to audit the substantial funding provided to section 38 and section 39 organisations; the processes used to ensure that such funding is allocated equitably in line with individual service plans; the oversight and governance systems in place to verify that public monies are being used appropriately; the mechanisms by which the HSE confirms that individuals for whom services are billed are in fact receiving those services; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [25674/26]

1182. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the supports currently in place, aside from available tax reliefs, to assist individuals diagnosed with coeliac disease in managing the additional healthcare and dietary costs associated with the condition; whether consideration is being given to further supports, including eligibility for a GP visit card or medical card, for those living with coeliac disease; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [37444/26]

582. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of HSE staff currently on sick leave or stress-related leave, by staff category; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18110/26]

583. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of cases of bullying reported by HSE staff in the most recent year for which data is available, broken down by hospital group, CHO area and staff category; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18111/26]

2821. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to provide the direct web link to the Health Service Executive's published purchase order data reports; the most recent quarter for which such data has been published; the date on which that report was published; and to outline the expected publication schedule for future reports. [24408/26]

2822. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to clarify where responses provided by the Health Service Executive to Parliamentary Questions, including replies issued directly to Deputies following referral from her Department, are published or made publicly accessible; and if such responses are not centrally available, whether consideration will be given to establishing a publicly accessible repository of such replies in the interest of transparency and consistency [24409/26]

829. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health further to Parliamentary Question No. 889 of 30 September 2025, and the subsequent direct reply from the Health Service Executive dated 14 October 2025 (details supplied), to provide the web link to the published dataset; the date on which the dataset was published; if the dataset has not been published, the reason for the delay; whether a revised publication date has been set; and if she will make a statement on the matter in addition to any response provided by the HSE. [47639/26]

840. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether she has satisfied herself that the commitment given by the Health Service Executive in its direct reply of 14 October 2025 to publish purchase order payment data for the period 2014 to Quarter 3 2021 in a machine-readable format has been fulfilled; and if not, the action that has been taken by her Department to secure publication of the data. [47671/26]

1936. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether the HSE maintains a national register of side letters, qualifications or reservations submitted by funded agencies in connection with service arrangements and grant aid agreements; if not, whether she will require the HSE to establish such a register; the formal response and corrective actions that have been taken in respect of the Comptroller and Auditor General's findings that such letters undermine the effectiveness of funding agreements and accountability for performance; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [76272/26]

1937. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether the HSE will publish, in CSV or Excel format, a complete annual breakdown of revenue and capital grant payments made to section 38, section 39, for-profit and out-of-State agencies for each of the years from 2016 to 2025, identifying the recipient, amount paid, year, grant category; whether the payment relates to revenue or capital expenditure; whether the HSE will commit to publishing this information quarterly from 2026 onwards; if not, the specific legal, technical or operational reasons preventing publication; and the date by which publication will commence. [76271/26]

380. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if the HSE is continuing to incur rental costs for portacabins located at Galway Airport that were put in place during the Covid-19 pandemic; if so, to provide a breakdown of all expenditure associated with these units, including rent, maintenance and any related costs, for each of the past six years, in tabular form; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [38663/26]

1750. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the status of the HSE and Department of Health assessment of Omaveloxolone (Skyclarys) for the treatment of Friedreich’s Ataxia; the timeline for completing the reimbursement process; the engagement that has taken place with patient representatives and clinical experts; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18744/26]

1751. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the specific steps the HSE is taking to ensure that the time-critical nature of Friedreich’s Ataxia is fully recognised and reflected in the ongoing price negotiations for the reimbursement of Skyclarys; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18745/26]

1752. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the way in which the commitments set out in the National Rare Disease Strategy 2025–2030, particularly regarding timely access to approved therapies for rare disease patients, are being applied to the current reimbursement process for Skyclarys for the treatment of Friedreich’s Ataxia; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18746/26]

1753. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the way in which the 180-day decision timeline contained within the 2026 IPHA Framework Agreement is being implemented in the case of Skyclarys, given that over 570 days have now elapsed since the reimbursement application was submitted; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [18747/26]

421. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if she will provide an update on the consideration by the HSE senior leadership team of the reimbursement application for givinostat; whether a decision has now been reached following the recommendation submitted by the Drugs Group on 9 June 2026; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [48421/26]

466. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the reason skyclarys has not been included on the agenda for the recent HSE Drugs Group meeting held in June 2026; when the drug will be considered by the Drugs Group; the timeline for a decision on its prioritisation within the reimbursement process; and the measures being taken to ensure there are no further avoidable delays in progressing access to skyclarys for patients living with Friedreich’s ataxia; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [48540/26]

473. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of schools currently registered under the Medicines for Listed Organisations framework to hold emergency medicines such as adrenaline auto-injectors for the treatment of severe allergic reactions; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [23373/26]

838. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether she is satisfied that current reimbursement timelines for orphan medicines align with the commitments on timely and equitable access set out in the National Rare Disease Strategy 2025–2030; the measures that are being taken to address delays in cases where EMA-approved treatments, including those for Friedreich’s ataxia, remain unavailable to patients in Ireland; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [31882/26]

795. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if she has engaged with the Minister for Finance regarding the application of VAT to certain vaccines and prescribed medical products; if changes are under consideration; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [51289/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether for procurement spend, a purchase order can be raised within her Department's financial management systems without reference to a contract, framework agreement, procurement process or other authorising arrangement; if so, the circumstances in which this may occur [45167/26]

886. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether an invoice can be paid by her Department without an associated purchase order having first been raised; if so, the circumstances in which this may occur; the number and value of payments made during quarter one of 2026 which were not associated with a purchase order; and if she will make a statement on the matter. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to provide the web link to her Department’s Q4 2025 published report of purchase orders/payments over €20,000, in line with the FOI model publication scheme requirements; the date on which this report was published; and if it has not yet been published, the planned publication date. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the total amount spent by her Department on public procurement in 2025; to provide a breakdown, where available, by goods, services, works procurement expenditure, by expenditure procured directly by her Department and expenditure procured through central purchasing arrangements or frameworks; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [42171/26]

1858. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to provide the web link to her Department’s Q3 2026 published report of purchase orders/payments over €20,000, in line with the FOI model publication scheme requirements; to confirm the date on which this report was published; and, if it has not yet been published, to state the planned publication date. [74720/25]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if she will review the current medical card income thresholds for those over 70 years of age, particularly in circumstances where household income includes carer's allowance and where there are high, recurring medical expenses; and the proposals to amend the existing assessment criteria. 791. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to review the means test thresholds for medical cards for persons aged over 70; if she will consider the introduction of universal medical card eligibility for those over 70; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [51285/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether her Department has considered measures to improve access to spare emergency medicines such as adrenaline auto-injectors in schools for use in cases of suspected but undiagnosed anaphylaxis; and if she will make a statement on the matter. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the number of persons who acquired a traumatic brain injury, neurological injury, long-term disability or other significant health condition as a result of being the victim of a physical assault in each of the past ten years; the number of such cases identified as arising from unprovoked assaults, where recorded; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [59863/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether the HSE, National Rehabilitation Hospital, Central Statistics Office, National Office for Trauma Services or any other public body collects data on acquired brain injuries resulting from assaults; if so, the number of cases recorded annually during the past 15 years; and if she will make a statement on the matter. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health to provide the web link to her Department’s Q1 2026 published report of purchase orders/payments over €20,000, in line with the FOI model publication scheme requirements; to confirm the date on which this report was published; and, if it has not yet been published, to state the planned publication date. [26911/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if her Department and each agency and public body under its aegis maintain a supplier register or equivalent electronic record in which suppliers are assigned unique identifiers; the identifier types held by each body, including CRO registration numbers, VAT numbers and internally generated supplier IDs; whether these identifiers are recorded against individual purchase orders, contracts and payments; and, where no such identifier is maintained, the way in which suppliers are uniquely identified within the body's financial and procurement systems, in tabular form. 1944. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if her Department and each agency and public body under its aegis publishes quarterly reports of purchase orders or payments over €20,000 in a machine-readable format such as CSV or XLSX; the bodies publishing only in PDF or other non-structured formats; the reasons for this, having regard to Regulation 7 of S.I. No. 376 of 2021; whether the underlying data is already held in a structured electronic format; and when publication in a machine-readable format will be introduced, in tabular form. [76249/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether purchase orders issued by her Department under procurement contracts can be linked to the corresponding contracts held in its internal contract register; whether a contract reference or other unique identifier is maintained to enable this linkage; and if not, the way her Department monitors cumulative expenditure against the approved value of each contract. [76996/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether contracts recorded in her Department's internal contract register can be linked to their corresponding contract award notices published on eTenders, where applicable; whether her Department records the relevant eTenders notice reference, URL or other identifier; and if not, the reasons that prevent this information from being recorded. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health whether her Department is fully compliant with the requirements of the Freedom of Information Model Publication Scheme Guidance, issued under section 8 of the Freedom of Information Act 2014, specifically the requirements under section D and section E (details supplied); to publish quarterly the contracts awarded above €25,000 (exclusive of VAT), including contract type, contractor, value, award date, duration and description, in tabular form; to provide the web links where this information is published; when her Department first became compliant with each applicable requirement; and if any applicable element has not yet been implemented in full, to outline the reasons, and any plans to achieve compliance. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health the measures she is taking to ensure continued access to dental care for medical card holders in light of the increasing number of dentists leaving the dental treatment services scheme due to financial unsustainability; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [47997/26]

Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Health if her attention has been drawn to reports that an organisation (details supplied) may be forced to cease operations due to funding difficulties; if her Department or the HSE are currently engaged with the organisation regarding funding or service continuity; the assessments made of the potential impact on access to low-cost counselling and gambling addiction supports should the service close; and if she will make a statement on the matter. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether his Department has engaged with the Department of Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation on the transfer of local authority pension liabilities to the Exchequer, or on a mechanism to fund local authority pension costs above a baseline amount; the dates and status of any such engagement; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [78394/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pensions
questions.question: 337. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether his Department has received any submission, business case or report from the County and City Management Association, the Local Government Management Agency or any local authority since 1 January 2022 concerning the funding of local authority pension and gratuity costs; the date of receipt of each; the response of his Department to each; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [78393/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pensions
questions.question: 338. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether his Department has received, commissioned or been made aware of any actuarial assessment of the liabilities of the local government superannuation scheme since 1 January 2022, including any assessment prepared by or on behalf of the local government sector; the date on which any such assessment was received; the estimated accrued liability and projected annual pension costs set out in it; and whether it will be published. [78392/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pensions
questions.question: 339. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether any Exchequer funding, recoupment or grant is provided to local authorities specifically towards the cost of pensions and gratuities under the local government superannuation scheme; and if so, the total amount provided in each of the years 2020 to 2025. [78391/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pay
questions.question: 340. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether funding provided to local authorities in respect of national public service pay agreements includes the consequent increase in the cost of pensions in payment arising from pay parity; if not, whether his Department has estimated that cost to local authorities; and the estimated cost in each of the years 2021 to 2025. [78390/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pensions
questions.question: 341. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage whether his Department compiles the Summary of Central Management Charge (Appendix 1) of local authority adopted budgets, including the pension and lump sum overhead, on a national basis; and if so, the amount provided in each local authority’s adopted budget under that heading for each of the years 2014 to 2026, in tabular form. [78389/26]

questions.heading: Public Sector Pensions
questions.question: 342. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the expenditure on pensions and gratuities, and the superannuation contributions received, as reported in the annual financial statements of each local authority for each of the years 2014 to 2025, by local authority, in tabular form. [78388/26]
